segments.speaker: SARAH
segments.en: Hello. Children’s Engineering Workshops.

segments.speaker: FATHER
segments.en: Oh hello. I wanted some information about the workshops in the school holidays.

segments.speaker: SARAH
segments.en: Sure.

segments.speaker: FATHER
segments.en: I have two daughters who are interested. The younger one’s Lydia, she’s four – do you take children as young as that?

segments.speaker: SARAH
segments.en: Yes, our Tiny Engineers workshop is for four to five-year-olds.

segments.speaker: FATHER
segments.en: What sorts of activities do they do?

segments.speaker: SARAH
segments.en: All sorts. For example, they work together to design a special cover that goes round an egg [[ ]] , so that when it’s inside they can drop it from a height and it doesn’t break. Well, sometimes it does break but that’s part of the fun!

segments.speaker: FATHER
segments.en: Right. And Lydia loves building things. Is there any opportunity for her to do that?

segments.speaker: SARAH
segments.en: Well, they have a competition to see who can make the highest tower [[ ]] . You’d be amazed how high they can go.

segments.speaker: FATHER
segments.en: Right.

segments.speaker: SARAH
segments.en: But they’re learning all the time as well as having fun. For example, one thing they do is to design and build a car [[ ]] that’s attached to a balloon, and the force of the air in that actually powers the car and makes it move along. They go really fast too.

segments.speaker: FATHER
segments.en: OK, well, all this sounds perfect. ————————–

segments.speaker: FATHER
segments.en: Now Carly, that’s my older daughter, has just had her seventh birthday, so presumably she’d be in a different group?

segments.speaker: SARAH
segments.en: Yes, she’d be in the Junior Engineers. That’s for children from six to eight.

segments.speaker: FATHER
segments.en: And do they do the same sorts of activities?

segments.speaker: SARAH
segments.en: Some are the same, but a bit more advanced. So they work out how to build model vehicles, things like cars and trucks, but also how to construct animals [[ ]] using the same sorts of material and technique, and then they learn how they can program them and make them move.

segments.speaker: FATHER
segments.en: So they learn a bit of coding?

segments.speaker: SARAH
segments.en: They do. They pick it up really quickly. We’re there to help if they need it, but they learn from one another too.

segments.speaker: FATHER
segments.en: Right. And do they have competition too?

segments.speaker: SARAH
segments.en: Yes, with the Junior Engineers, it’s to use recycled materials like card and wood to build a bridge [[ ]] , and the longest one gets a prize.

segments.speaker: FATHER
segments.en: That sounds fun. I wouldn’t mind doing that myself!

segments.speaker: SARAH
segments.en: Then they have something a bit different, which is to think up an idea for a five-minute movie [[ ]] and then film it, using special animation software. You’d be amazed what they come up with.

segments.speaker: FATHER
segments.en: And of course, that’s something they can put on their phone and take home to show all their friends.

segments.speaker: SARAH
segments.en: Exactly. And then they also build a robot in the shape of a human, and they decorate [[ ]] it and program it so that it can move its arms and legs.

segments.speaker: FATHER
segments.en: Perfect. So, is it the same price as the Tiny Engineers?

segments.speaker: SARAH
segments.en: It’s just a bit more: £50 for the five weeks.

segments.speaker: FATHER
segments.en: And are the classes on a Monday, too?

segments.speaker: SARAH
segments.en: They used to be, but we found it didn’t give our staff enough time to clear up after the first workshop, so we moved them to Wednesdays [[ ]] . The classes are held in the morning from ten to eleven.

segments.speaker: FATHER
segments.en: OK. That’s better for me actually. And what about the location? Where exactly are the workshops held?

segments.speaker: SARAH
segments.en: They’re in building 10A – there’s a big sign on the door, you can’t miss it, and that’s in Fradstone [[ ]] Industrial Estate.

segments.speaker: FATHER
segments.en: Sorry?

segments.speaker: SARAH
segments.en: Fradstone – that’s F-R-A-D-S-T-O-N-E.

segments.speaker: FATHER
segments.en: And that’s in Grasford, isn’t it?

segments.speaker: SARAH
segments.en: Yes, up past the station.

segments.speaker: FATHER
segments.en: And will I have any parking [[ ]] problems there?

segments.speaker: SARAH
segments.en: No, there’s always plenty available. So would you like to enrol Lydia and Carly now?

segments.speaker: FATHER
segments.en: OK.

segments.speaker: SARAH
segments.en: So can I have your full name ...
